label: Aggregate operator pushdown (the sub-family)
type: the sub-family covering the individual aggregate operators the Indexer can compute directly: MIN, MAX, COUNT and COUNT DISTINCT. Sits under index:index-pushdown and overlaps index:group-aggregate-pushdown, which implements these through the same `index_group_aggs` plan field.
recurrence_note: ONE independent source for the collecting term itself (3 files discounted to 1, `shared`, discount upheld), which is below the bar. Promoted under the reconcile skill's family exception, stated here rather than applied silently. The MEMBERS are better attested than the family that contains them: n1ql:min-pushdown and n1ql:max-pushdown are at 3 files each and BOTH come back `divergent`, so their counts stand undiscounted, while n1ql:count-pushdown and n1ql:count-distinct-pushdown sit at 1 each.
aliases_note: `index:min-pushdown` and `index:max-pushdown` were listed here in this record's first draft and have MOVED to the two members' own records, which is where an alias for a separately promoted term belongs - two records claiming one alias would make alias resolution ambiguous. The two remaining aliases stay here because n1ql:count-pushdown and n1ql:count-distinct-pushdown are at 1 file each and are NOT separately promoted, so this record is the only place a lookup can land.
members: n1ql:count-pushdown (1 file, not promoted; covered by this record)
n1ql:count-distinct-pushdown (1 file, not promoted; covered by this record)
members_note: A CORRECTION TO THIS RECORD'S FIRST DRAFT. It was filed at recurrence 1 under the family exception while stating, in `recurrence_note`, that min and max sit at 3 divergent files each - i.e. clear the bar on the mechanical rule - and it left them unfiled. That is the promotion rule applied upside down: the below-bar collecting term got a record and the above-bar members did not, so an agent reusing `n1ql:min-pushdown` would truthfully declare `extraction-layer` for a term reconciliation had already decided about. A `members` list is not reachable by alias resolution and does not stand in for a record. Both are now filed under `concepts/n1ql/`; the family record still earns its place, because it is what makes COUNT and COUNT DISTINCT - genuinely at 1 file each - reachable at all.
note:
PROMOTED AS A FAMILY, AND IT RESOLVES THE ROUND'S UGLIEST NAMESPACE FORK. The four operators are spelled `n1ql:` in the extraction layer while every term that groups them is spelled `index:`, so the family and its members live in different namespaces. Round 16's rule is that `index:` takes anything true of indexes, pushdowns included, which would make all four `index:*`.
RESOLVED BY ALIASING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS RATHER THAN REWRITING, deliberately. The `index:` spellings are recorded as aliases of this family record so a future agent looking up either form finds one place; the `n1ql:` ids remain the members' canonical names because that is what 593 records on disk actually say. Rewriting six ids across the extraction layer to satisfy a naming rule is a migration, and it would also destroy the evidence that the fork ever happened - which is the only reason anyone knows the promotion metric was deflated here. One deliberate move over six ids, as the extracting agent put it, and not six independent judgement calls.
WHY THE FORK MATTERED RATHER THAN JUST BEING UNTIDY: a fork splits one term's files across two rows, so a genuine candidate sits below the bar TWICE and reads as two weak terms instead of one adequate one. `recurrence.py --forks` exists because of this family. Sixteen rounds had an instrument for the opposite error (shared source inflating a count) and none for this one.
VERSION HISTORY HAS BEEN DELETED FROM THE SOURCE, which affects what this record can claim. The 7.2 page dated the MIN/MAX descending-index-key limitation to 5.5 in two sentences; the 8.0 page replaced both with an undated statement. The existing server/7.2 extraction record therefore asserts `availableSince version:server-5-5` on a sentence that no longer exists in the current release. That relation is still true history and is NOT withdrawn - but it is no longer verifiable against 8.0, and an 8.0-only reader cannot learn that the limitation ever existed. See docs-issues/server-index-pushdowns-version-facts-removed.
